description.p: Use MergeFX to composite multiple input sources so that they are rendered on top of each other in a predefined sequence.

Many effects produce a number of intermediate layers in order to create the final output image. This filter allows us to collapse those into a single image. Although this could be done by using n-1 Composite-filters, it is more convenient to have this common operation available in this form, and offers the implementation some additional flexibility.

field.name: Layers
field.comment: An ordered list of weighted merge sources, from bottom to top.

description.p: The list is an array of MergeLayer structures. Each layer is composited over the result of the layers before it, so the first entry is the bottom of the stack. Assigning an array replaces the entire list. The new list is validated before it is applied, so the existing list is retained if an error is returned.

A REFERENCE layer requires the EffectID of an earlier effect in the same filter. The EffectID is reset to zero for all other source types. A layer with a SourceType of NONE contributes nothing to the result. The Opacity scales the alpha channel of the source before it is composited, and must be in the range 0 - 1. Enabled must be 1 to render the layer or 0 to skip it.
Disabled layers and layers with an Opacity of 0 retain their configuration but are not rendered and do not read their source. This allows layers to be toggled without rebuilding the list.

If a referenced effect is removed from the filter, the EffectID of its layer is reset to zero and the SourceType remains REFERENCE. Assign a new list to repair the pipeline. Reading SourceList returns the same sources without the Opacity and Enabled controls.
In SVG documents, each feMergeNode defines a layer. The xvg:opacity attribute sets the Opacity and xvg:enabled="false" disables the layer.

field.name: SourceList
field.comment: A list of source types to be processed in the merge.

description.p: The list is an array of MergeSource structures. Reading it returns the bindings from Layers in order. Assigning it replaces Layers with enabled entries at opacity one.

Input sources are defined by the SourceType field value. A REFERENCE entry needs a pointer to an earlier effect in the same filter before the pipeline can render. If a referenced effect is removed, that entry retains its REFERENCE type and its pointer is cleared. Replace the list to repair the pipeline.
